title: API version handshake + v1 deprecation shim for compatibility layer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce runtime shim to accept legacy v1-style requests and emit deprecation warnings
Stabilize streaming framing for structured output to avoid partial JSON chunks
Docs: migration guide and deprecation timeline
description:
Context: Customers using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint expect stability across minor schema changes, but several recent server-side improvements (structured output framing, function-calling key normalization, and explicit streaming markers) require a controlled transition. This PR introduces a server-side API version handshake and a v1-compatible shim so clients without the new beta header continue to work, combined with an explicit deprecation path and migration warnings.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds support for an opt-in header X-Redwood-Api-Version set to 'v2-beta' which enables new structured-output framing semantics and normalized function/tool-calling payloads. When the header is absent or set to 'v1' the runtime will run the v1-compat shim that: 1) preserves legacy streaming chunk boundaries (no extra framing bytes), 2) accepts both 'tool_call' and 'function_call' as synonyms for function invocation, and 3) maps new structured-output envelope fields back to the older flat shape expected by v1 SDKs. The shim also injects a deprecation warning into response metadata and emits an audit log entry (compat_v1_deprecation_warn) once per client session.

Motivation: We have observed increased customer breakage after introducing structured-output framing changes in the hosted runtime and in downstream SDKs. Rather than forcing an immediate global migration, this change enables a short-lived compatibility mode so we can roll out RT fixes and give clients progressive opt-in via the header. The approach reduces incident risk while allowing us to iterate on v2 semantics (framing, deterministic JSON boundaries for streaming, and stricter function schema) behind an explicit opt-in.

Key design points: - Header-based opt-in: X-Redwood-Api-Version: v2-beta enables the new behavior. The header is case-insensitive and accepted via both REST and websocket protocols. - Non-op shim: When running in v1-compat mode the shim performs minimal transformations and strictly avoids changing model outputs. Only wire-level framing and field renames are applied. - Deprecation cadence: v1 compatibility mode will be supported for 180 days from the merge date; deprecation telemetry will track client usage by client_id. - Streaming stability: New framing uses explicit record separators (0x1E) between well-formed JSON chunks so downstream stream parsers can reliably split messages without partial-JSON assembly (addresses flakiness in streaming parsers observed in SUP-412). v1-compat retains legacy delimiter behavior. - Tool/function calling: The shim accepts new-style function_call objects but converts them to the legacy tool_call.{name,args} shape expected by older SDKs. It also tolerates both camelCase and snake_case keys. - Diagnostics: Adds per-request header X-Compat-Warn in responses when shimned, and emits a structured log line in the audit-log-exporter topic for infra analytics.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime: handshake parsing and shim implementation (runtime/compat/shim.go)
- [x] API gateway: header passthrough + validation (gateway/headers.go)
- [x] Docs: migration guide and deprecation notes (docs/openai-compat/migration.md)
- [x] SDK test matrix updated (sdk-tests/compat)
- [x] E2E: streaming stability tests updated and flaky parser regression fixed (tests/streaming/structured_output_test.go)
- [x] Telemetry: compat usage counter and deprecation logs (telemetry/compat.go)

Rollout plan: Merge to main, feature-flag off for immediate rollout. Flip feature flag for 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor compat usage and streaming error rates, then progressive ramp. After 30 days post-ramp start broadcast migration warnings to client owners and mark deprecated_clients in Linear.

Notes on implementation tradeoffs: We intentionally avoided altering model output tokens; transformations are strictly at the wire/schema level. This avoids subtle regressions where token-level changes would alter prompts or downstream evals. The shim is intentionally small and localized to minimize maintenance burden.

Related: SUP-412 (streaming parser flakiness), ENG-2041 (structured output initiative), ENG-2103 (function calling normalization).
